verdicts.strongest_argument: The conclusion of this claim - that the Q1 gross-margin shortfall was one-time launch inefficiency and not a commodity problem, so margins revert to the mid-to-high 20s - is management's own publicly stated guidance from the June 8 call, echoed across every earnings summary (StockTitan, GuruFocus, Yahoo, Motley Fool). The CFO explicitly quantified the ~$0.5-1.0m one-time labour/material inefficiency and the ~$0.5m marketing-to-trade reclass, and guided margins back to target 'as new product launches transition from startup phase to steady-state.' The market has had this since June 8. What is genuinely obscure and unpriced is the commodity leg itself - CME block cheddar at $1.505 near the bottom of its range and boneless breast at $4.15/lb - which no MAMA-facing coverage connects; but that is a secondary confirmation of an already-published margin-recovery thesis, not the driver, and cheese/chicken were never the reason the market de-rated the stock.

prior_publication.what_it_says: Q1 gross margin fell to 23.6% on launch/labour/material inefficiency; management guides margins back to mid-to-high 20% target as launches reach steady state.
CME 40-lb block cheddar closed $1.505/lb on July 8, near the low end of its multi-year range.

verdicts.baseline_evidence: Genuine earnings amc dates reconstructed from the history array: 2026-06-08 (-11.12%), 2026-04-14 (-0.32%), 2025-12-08 (+28.09%, Q3 beat), 2025-09-08 (-4.93%), 2025-06-03 (+0.72%), so genuine earnings moves cluster small-to-mid with occasional large beats; I did not use the contaminated 6.08% median or the non-earnings 2025-09-02/03-11 bmo rows. The -11.12% June reaction shows the market already saw and de-rated the margin miss; recovery language is management-supplied.
verdicts.what_would_change_it: If the Q2 print showed a margin recovery whose magnitude is well beyond the guided mid-to-high 20s and specifically attributable to the commodity tailwind, the obscure leg would carry real residual.

verdicts.strongest_argument: The central evidence is a sentence management said aloud on the June 8 call - 'the cost is all in Q1... very little of the revenue was in Q1' - which is public by construction and was carried verbatim in the Motley Fool/Globe and Mail transcript plus every earnings recap. The favourable cost-then-revenue split across the Q1/Q2 boundary is therefore the obvious, publicly telegraphed setup for exactly this print; it is the consensus bull framing, not hidden. The claim's own 'market sold the stock 15.8% with no company news' is weak evidence of mispricing: the 20-session decline is far better explained by the 5.56m-share/$94m dilution priced June 29-July 1 (offering struck at $18 vs current $15.37, ~13% dilution) plus digestion of the Q1 miss and small-cap food weakness, not by the market failing to notice a transcript quote it has had for three months.

prior_publication.what_it_says: Management states the Walmart/Target deli launch costs were incurred in Q1 while the revenue lands in Q2.
MAMA completed a $18.00 equity offering raising ~$94m, diluting existing holders - a concrete cause of the 20-session decline the claim attributes to mispricing.

verdicts.baseline_evidence: Run-up 20d -15.81% coincides with the June 29-July 1 dilution window, undercutting the 'sold into the split with no news' premise. Options are effectively dead (526 total OI, 55%-of-mid ATM spread) so give no signal on whether the Q2 flow-through is priced.
verdicts.what_would_change_it: If MAMA has genuinely no sell-side model reflecting the Q2 revenue step-up (near-zero coverage) and Q2 revenue/margin materially exceed the mechanical flow-through, the thin-coverage residual would justify a lower number.
verdicts.prior_publication_note: transcript fully public and widely covered

verdicts.strongest_argument: The $94m raise 'to fund the acquisition of businesses or other assets' is fully public and was reported everywhere June 30-July 1 (TipRanks, Globe and Mail, StockTitan, TradingView); the market plainly knows MAMA has M&A firepower and an acquisitive posture, and the Crown I precedent is on EDGAR. So the dry-powder/intent is priced. What is not priced is a specific, unannounced deal landing in this calendar slot - but that is unpriceable by nature rather than missed, and its mechanism to THIS print is speculative: an acquisition is a separate 8-K item 1.01/2.01 that may or may not coincide with the earnings date. The claim leans on low option open interest as evidence the optionality is unpriced, but on a chain with only 526 total contracts and a 55%-of-mid ATM spread, low OI means nobody trades these options at all - not that the market formed and dismissed an M&A view. I therefore read the dead chain as no evidence either way, not as confirmation of hidden upside.

prior_publication.what_it_says: MAMA completed the offering, ~$94m net, earmarked for working capital and complementary acquisitions - the M&A firepower is public.
Prior-year Crown I asset purchase plus $20m placement filed six days before the Q2 print; the pattern the claim relies on is itself on public EDGAR.

No 8-K item 1.01/2.01 visible since the raise.
verdicts.what_would_change_it: If MAMA actually files or pre-announces an acquisition with/near tonight's print, the specific-deal residual is large; absent that, the priceable content is just the already-public dry powder.

verdicts.strongest_argument: The Albertsons datapoint is fully public and heavily covered - the July 23 guidance cut (FY ID-sales to -1.5%/-0.5%, EBITDA to $3.55-3.625bn, -0.8% comps for the 16 weeks ended June 20) ran in Drug Store News, Shelby Report, Motley Fool and Albertsons' own release the same day. So the raw fact is priced into ACI and into the broadly-known 'cautious consumer' theme that already sits on small-cap food names. The MAMA read-through is nowhere drawn out explicitly, so that inference is unpriced - but it is weak in magnitude: MAMA grew Q1 revenue 49.7% on new-door rollout (Walmart 2,000 / Target 750 / Food Lion), which is distribution-driven, and a single perimeter customer's -0.8% same-store drift is immaterial against ~50% idiosyncratic growth. The bearish mechanism barely reaches this print.

prior_publication.what_it_says: Albertsons cut FY2026 ID-sales and EBITDA guidance citing softer unit trends and a more cautious consumer; -0.8% ID sales for the 16 weeks ended June 20.

verdicts.baseline_evidence: No skew available (25d skew null, chain near-dead), so I cannot claim downside is bid via options. The -15.81% 20d run-up already embeds macro/consumer caution, so some of this theme is in the tape - but as broad de-rating, not a MAMA-specific Albertsons read.
verdicts.what_would_change_it: If MAMA's revenue were comp-driven at mature Albertsons banners rather than new-door-driven, the -0.8% read-through would be material; evidence of soft velocity at existing deli doors would raise this.
verdicts.prior_publication_note: Albertsons news fully public; MAMA read-through unpublished but small

interactions: MAMA#0 and MAMA#1 rest on the same June 8 transcript and are mirror framings of one thesis - the Q1-heavy cost / Q2-heavy revenue split and the resulting margin recovery; collapse them to a single margin-recovery residual, with #0 carrying only the small extra obscure-commodity leg on top of #1. Separately, MAMA#1 ('no company news since the 2026-08-20 earnings-date notice') and MAMA#2 ('filed no 8-K item 1.01/2.01 in two months') both rest on the same observation of the EDGAR filing index - the absence of filings after a given date. That absence is weak evidence in a specific way: EDGAR is fully public, so the market is not missing the fact that no deal has been announced; the empty filing index is the base state everyone can see, not hidden information, which is why I did not let the 'no filings' leg pull either number down toward genuinely-unpriced. Net: the cluster's largest residual is the speculative timing of an actual acquisition (MAMA#2), and even that is optionality that may not land in this print's window.
